{"code": "import pandas as pd

# Load the data
df = pd.read_csv('data/sales.csv')

# Confirm the data dictionary's claim about QA orders
qa_orders = df[df['revenue'] == '999999.99']
print(f"Total QA orders in the dataset: {len(qa_orders)}")

# Check if any QA orders are in the loyal_completed group
loyal_completed = df[(df['customer_segment'] == 'loyal') & (df['status'] == 'completed')]
qa_in_loyal = loyal_completed[loyal_completed['revenue'] == '999999.99']
print(f"QA orders in loyal completed group: {len(qa_in_loyal)}")

# Inspect one QA order
columns = ['order_id', 'channel', 'customer_segment', 'customer_age', 'status', 'revenue', 'converted']
if len(qa_in_loyal) > 0:
    print(qa_in_loyal[columns].iloc[0])
else:
    print("No QA orders found in loyal completed group.")

# Check for any other anomalies
print(f"Number of refunded orders: {(df['status'] == 'refunded').sum()}")
print(f"Number of -1 in customer_age: {(df['customer_age'] == -1).sum()}")"}
